title: Microsoft Purview: audit records for role and scoped-role permission checks
summary: The briefing's audit operations, default state and rollout dates agree with Microsoft's notice, and the cited control documentation opens successfully. Two minor corrections remain: identify the published general Audit licensing entitlement and extend the role-group path to the membership control.

claims.claim: This change concerns Microsoft Purview role and scoped-role permission-check audit records.
claims.quote: Enhanced audit logs will provide clearer visibility into role and scoped-role access decisions

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Searching or exporting audit records requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in the Purview portal.
claims.quote: Admins and members of investigation teams must be assigned the View-Only Audit Logs or Audit Logs role in the Microsoft Purview portal to search or export the audit log.

claims.claim: Restricted administrators can search and export only user-generated audit logs within their assigned administrative units.
claims.quote: A restricted admin can only search and export user-generated audit logs within the scope of their assigned administrative units.

claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators can access all audit logs, including non-user and system-account logs.
claims.quote: An unrestricted admin has access to all audit logs, including logs generated by non-user and system accounts.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not specify whether restricted administrators can see these two new operation records.
claims.quote: Searched: "CheckUserInRolesWithScopes" administrative units fields retention; "CheckUsersInRoles" "CheckUserInRolesWithScopes" audit fields licensing retention administrative units. Opened Audit search and RBAC schema; neither identifies the new records' scoping or generating identity.

claims.claim: An Entra role takes precedence over a scoped Purview role-group assignment for overlapping capabilities, leaving those capabilities unscoped.
claims.quote: When both scoped Microsoft Purview role assignments and Entra roles are present, Entra roles always take precedence, and scoping applied through Administrative Units doesn't restrict the user's effective permissions for overlapping capabilities.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no requirement specific to the two new audit operations is published.
claims.quote:
| Feature | Microsoft 365 E3/A3/A1/G3/F3/F1 | Office 365 E3/E1/A3/A1/G3/G1/F3 | Microsoft 365 Business Basic/Standard/Premium |
| Audit (Standard) | Included | Included | Included |
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the opening licensing explanation with: 'General Audit licensing applies: Audit (Standard) is included in Microsoft 365 E3 and Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Standard and Premium, among other listed plans. Microsoft has not published a separate licence requirement for these two new operations.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description and retain the existing per-user and retention qualifications. Use the same narrower wording in licensing.notes and the cost rationale.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price specific to the two new audit operations.
claims.quote: Searched: "CheckUsersInRoles" licensing price meter. Opened Audit get started, auditing solutions overview and Microsoft Purview service description; they describe general Audit licensing, not a price for either new operation.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter specific to the two new audit operations.
claims.quote: Searched: "CheckUsersInRoles" licensing price meter. Opened Audit get started, auditing solutions overview and Microsoft Purview service description; no meter for either permission-check operation was found.

claims.claim: MC1473155 does not mention a charge.
claims.quote: The enhancement is enabled by default and requires no configuration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: General Audit licensing requires an appropriate organisation subscription.
claims.quote: Licensing for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium) requires the appropriate organization subscription that provides access to the audit log search tool

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: General Audit licensing requires the per-user licensing needed to log and retain audit records.
claims.quote: per-user licensing that's required to log and retain audit records.

claims.claim: Audit retention and searchability depend on the subscription and the licence assigned to particular users.
claims.quote: The length of time that an audit record is retained (and searchable in the audit log) depends on your Office 365 or Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription, and specifically the type of the license that is assigned to specific users.

claims.claim: The general Audit (Standard) retention period is 180 days.
claims.quote: In Audit (Standard), the system retains records for 180 days, which means you can search for activities that occurred within the past six months.

claims.claim: Audit (Premium) defaults to 180 days for activities outside Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.quote: It retains all Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra audit records for one year. ... Audit records for all other activities are retained for 180 days by default

claims.claim: Applicable retention policies can change the general default retention for user-generated records.
claims.quote: Audit records for all other activities are retained for 180 days by default or you can change the retention to a different duration using a custom retention policy.

claims.claim: Audit records generated by non-user entities have a separate fixed one-year retention rule.
claims.quote: Audit records generated by non-user entities (such as service principal actions, system events, and application activities) are retained for a fixed period of one year.

claims.claim: The new operations' workload and generating identity are not documented sufficiently to select a retention rule.
claims.quote: Searched: "CheckUserInRolesWithScopes" administrative units fields retention; "CheckUsersInRoles" "CheckUserInRolesWithScopes" audit fields licensing retention administrative units. Opened Audit log activities, RBAC schema and retention policies; no operation-specific workload or identity found.

Platforms and services

claims.claim: General audit logging is on by default for Microsoft 365 organisations, subject to the stated SMB exception.

claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses, including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium.

claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results.

claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig piped to Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled checks auditing status in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To verify that auditing is turned on for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell:
Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first row; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal Audit solution opens the Search page used to search the audit log.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog accepts StartDate, EndDate and a comma-separated Operations filter containing the two notice-supplied names.
claims.quote:
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime>
... [-Operations <String[]>]
The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation. ... You can enter multiple values separated by commas.

claims.claim: Activities - operations names is the audit search field for exact operation names.
claims.quote: Activities - operations names: Enter the exact operation names to search for audited activities to include in your search results. You can enter one or more operation names, separated by commas.

claims.claim: Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups is the Purview route for managing who can search and export the audit log.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. ... select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the matching rendered cell to 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users'. The existing path reaches the correct role-group list but stops before its membership control.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity <role group name> -Member <user> grants the selected group's permissions through membership.
claims.quote:
Add-RoleGroupMember
    [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter>
    -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter>
When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.

claims.claim: Audit Reader and Audit Manager are the default role groups assigned the audit search roles.
claims.quote: By default, the Microsoft Purview portal Role groups page assigns these roles to the Audit Reader and Audit Manager role groups.

claims.claim: Viewing Purview role groups requires Global Administrator or Role Management.
claims.quote: To view Role groups in the Roles and scopes area in the Microsoft Purview portal, users need to be a global administrator or need to be assigned the Role Management role

claims.claim: Audit > Start recording user and admin activity in the Purview portal enables auditing.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns on auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing.
Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: The start-recording banner appears when tenant auditing is off.
claims.quote: If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.

claims.claim: Learn documents turning auditing off through Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Use Exchange Online PowerShell to turn off auditing.
... Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $false

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Compliance Management and Organization Management hold the Exchange Online Audit Logs role by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Compliance Management and Organization Management role groups on the Permissions page in the Exchange admin center have this role.

claims.claim: Learn documents no setting specific to the two new permission-check operations at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview permissions audit CheckUsersInRoles enable disable Set-AdminAuditLogConfig; site:learn.microsoft.com/purview "CheckUsersInRoles". Opened Turn auditing on or off, permissions, audit activities and RBAC schema; no operation-specific switch found.

claims.claim: The tenant unified audit control affects audit logging generally, not just these two operations.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results. Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is run in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: The Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet is available in Exchange Online PowerShell.
